event.description: Use one eight-dimensional attention head with a learned residual projection
event.proposal: Family: attention organization. Current retained frontier is 1,672 parameters at 99.010000%, a +0.010000 percentage-point margin over 99%. There have been 9 prior attempts in this family. The most recent accepted result is attempt-0020, which removed attention output projections and qualified at 3,168 parameters and 99.94%; the most recent failed result is attempt-0102, whose global rank-6 value map scored 0.00% at 1,657 parameters. Hypothesis: two distinct attention maps may be redundant if one full eight-dimensional head can redistribute its attended values through a learned 8x16 residual projection. This major attention substitution retains the first checkpoint head's full Q/K/V rows, adds a learned output projection initialized as its original residual embedding, shares both transforms across depth, and yields 1,465 parameters. It is more informative than simply deleting a head because the learned projection preserves the ability to write into every residual coordinate and isolates the number of attention maps rather than output dimensionality. Causal softmax self-attention, feed-forward paths, representations, autoregressive logits, and generic decoding remain intact.
